Here's how I explained it to my daughter- who will be dealing with student loans before too much longer. Let's say you had a lemonade stand. On a warm sunny day, you might get a dollar or so for a glass of lemonade. If you tried charging $20 for a glass of lemonade, you'd never sell a glass. But if you tell your customers that they have to buy lemonade to make it through the rest of the day and that someone else will pay the up front cost and that the customer has 20 years to pay it back, what happens to the price? $100 for a glass? Why not? $500? Who cares, right? You need it and don't have to pay for it right away.

So one thing, certainly not the only thing, that will happen is that college tuition will bottom out. There's no difference between 10K and 10M a year in tuition if you can't pay either. Of course, colleges need money to run. Several things are likely to happen. Public universities will become government funded. This is not necessarily a good thing, despite hype. I've seen what happens behind the scenes when schools begin taking money from the government. I'm a double-TK (Teacher's Kid) and have seen the curriculum in two different schools ruined because they began taking money from the government and suddenly had to cut out parts of their curriculum to add in things like federally-mandated drug awareness programs.

More expensive private universities- Ivy League, MIT, etc- will likely expand on the student aid programs that they already have in place. And it wouldn't surprise me if schools started dipping into that vast ocean of money that runs their football and basketball programs and use it for other purposes. Dunno on that one, though.
